text:
sara chen: @here getting pages from EDGE-MEX1, multiple customers reporting high tail latency and 502s. alert: edge-pop-mex1-http-5xx-rate > 3% over 5m. Can someone from netops pick this up?

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-6017. Severity: P1. Paging on-call. Runbook: edge-pop-degradation.

miguel ramos: ack, I'm oncall. seeing packet loss from our eBGP peers into mex1 POP. Nagios/metrics show RTT jumps and retransmits on the mex1-egress veth.

kevin choi: copied. customers: a couple of video clients and a SaaS customer in MX-CP region showing heavy retransmits. Any evidence it's CDN-internal vs last-mile?

miguel ramos: initial tcpdump from mex1-cdn01 shows bursty 3-5% packet loss on the egress to IX provider:
```
# tcpdump -i eth2 -w /tmp/mex1-loss.pcap
14:03:12 IP 10.0.0.1 > 203.0.113.45: Flags [.], seq 1:1439, ack 1, win 42, length 1438
... retransmit ...
```

tara li: monitoring shows 502 spike aligned with ISP loss windows, cache hit ratio unchanged, so likely last-mile. I can try steering away from that egress to alternative transit.

miguel ramos: agree. preparing to withdraw specific /24 via local BGP community to prefer backup transit. Plan: 1) reduce DNS TTL for mx edge records to 30s 2) BGP withdraw primary egress and advertise via backup transit 3) enable connection-level retry/failover at edge for 5m window.

kevin choi: customer-impact note: CS reported 8 customers escalated, about ~2.3% of total requests from LATAM. Add to incident header.

customer-success: on it — I'm contacting the top-3 affected accounts and prepping a short status note. ETA 10m.

miguel ramos: BGP commands I'm running:
```
# show ip bgp neighbors 203.0.113.1 advertised-routes | match 198.51.100.0/24
198.51.100.0/24 next-hop 10.0.1.1 metric 0
# neighbor 203.0.113.1 soft-reconfig inbound
# route-map SET-BACKUP permit 10
# set local-preference 50
```
Executing community to de-preference primary.

netops-bot: BGP change applied to mx-routers. Change-id: bgp-change-4372. Route advertisements updated.

miguel ramos: Confirming traffic shift — partial shift visible, tail latency improved in metrics after route change. Graph: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/edge/mex1-egress?panel=5 (private).

kevin choi: Can we also lower DNS TTL for mx-edge.redwood.ai to 30s so cached clients retry quickly? Ops: set via Route53 zone, I'll do it.

tara li: I'll enable connection-level retry and increase request timeouts for mex1 pools for 5 minutes to allow graceful rollover. Config snippet:
```
edge.config.routes[mex1].retry = { attempts: 3, backoffMs: 200 }
edge.config.routes[mex1].timeoutMs = 12000
```

miguel ramos: netflow shows most flows are now hitting backup transit, packetloss dropped below 0.5% on new path. Watching for flaps.

incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by miguel ramos. On-call handoff note added.

customer-success: Sent preliminary status to affected customers: "We're seeing regional last-mile packet loss affecting Mexico POP. We're diverting traffic to alternate transit and expect reduced errors within 10-15 minutes."

kevin choi: ops note: TTL lowered to 30s on edge hostnames. Also incremented cache revalidation window to avoid burst to origin.

tara li: load test quick check: simulated clients now show 99th p95 latency back to normal for the past 3m. 502 rate down to 0.4%. Will keep 5m mitigation window then reevaluate.

miguel ramos: still seeing a small number of long-tail errors for a minority of ASN paths — likely the ISP is reconfiguring. I've opened a ticket with IX provider (ticket #MX-7892) and asked for BFD/phys port check.

customer-success: will follow up with customers once we hit steady-state.

kevin choi: suggestion: add a temporary traffic steering rule to keep mex1-origin > backup transit for 30m to avoid oscillation while ISP stabilizes. miguel, ok to keep BGP community applied?

miguel ramos: yes keeping for 30m. set rollback timer in 40m to revert if no issues.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-15-6017 status: mitigation in progress. Next update in 10 minutes or on major change.

sara chen: thanks all — good fast runbook execution. tagging to postmortem team for RCA capture. If anyone sees reappearance, ping on this thread and we'll escalate to sev2.handoff.

miguel ramos: final note before handing off: backup path stable, error rate < 0.5%, closing immediate impact window. Leaving bgp-change in place for 30m. I'll update incident timeline and hand to next oncall in 40m.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: MONITORING. Assigned: miguel ramos.

sara chen: closing oncall page for now. thanks.
